significance: A sunken temple on 2nd Temple Street in Malleswaram, built as a pillared corridor around a stepped tank, in which water runs constantly from the mouth of an unusual south-facing Nandi onto the lingam below. Buried for centuries, it was uncovered in 1997 when residents opposed building work on the plot and the ground was excavated.
story: The spring feeding the tank is held to be the sacred source of the river Vrishabhavati.
